content: Plan: Forecaster -> Uncertainty <-> Critic (revision loop) -> Critic risk -> Planner.
Loaded 6,435 rows, 45 series, source=walmart_synthetic.
Goal: forecast demand 2 periods ahead for 45 series. Every sales-derived feature must be at least that old, otherwise the evaluation leaks the future.
Built 18 features; chronological split train < 2012-01-13, validation to 2012-07-13, test to 2012-10-26.
Trained hist_gbm model on 4,185 training rows.
Top demand drivers (permutation importance): store_code, roll_mean_4, roll_mean_13, week_of_year, lag_4, month
Running the classical ETS baseline (rolling origin) over validation + test; it is both a benchmark and a blend candidate.
Held-out validation WAPE: gbm 0.038, blend 0.037, seasonal_naive 0.045, ets 0.042; blend weight on the model chosen on the calibration window = 0.8.
Using 'blend' (validation WAPE 0.037; 18% lower than seasonal naive).
-> Uncertainty: 1,890 forecasts ready (validation + test).
Goal: 90% prediction intervals. Counts get noisier as demand grows, so residuals are scaled by sqrt(forecast+1) and calibrated per series with shrinkage to the global value.
Calibrated on 810 validation rows (the last 8 validation days are held back for the Critic).
-> Critic: Intervals ready. Please check coverage on the held-out validation window.
Coverage on the held-out validation window is 92.5% (target 90%); bias -1.1%.
Calibration approved: intervals are honest enough to drive safety stock.
Re-fitted the calibrator on the full validation window (1,170 rows) and applied interval scale x1.00.

Errors on consecutive days are correlated, so multi-period demand is more uncertain than independent daily sigmas suggest: the standardised error of P-period sums has std 1.03 on validation. Planner sigma will be inflated by x1.03.
Reliability scores computed per series (1 - validation WAPE). Least reliable: W38, W01, W23.
-> Critic: Final intervals and sigma ready for shock assessment.

Three signals are checked for every series-period: (1) calendar events, (2) weather far outside the training climate for series that are weather-sensitive, in the direction that raises demand, (3) recent forecast errors that are worse than during validation. Each raises the risk multiplier.
Weather sensitivity learned from training data (pooled by series_id): 0 of 45 series (0%) react to temperature anomalies; only those can receive a weather flag.

Risk weights learned from validation errors and shrunk towards the hand-set priors: event 0.18 (prior 0.25, n=45), weather 0.35 (prior 0.35, n=0), price 0.20 (prior 0.20, n=0), drift 0.23 (prior 1.25, n=443).
Test window: 6.2% of series-periods have an event flag, 0.0% a weather flag, 27.4% an error-drift flag, 0.0% a price flag; mean risk multiplier 1.08.
Risk multipliers published to the Uncertainty agent (interval widening) and the Planner (safety stock).
-> Uncertainty: Risk assessment complete; widen intervals on flagged days.
Widened intervals on Critic-flagged days (half-width x risk multiplier); 21.9% of test series-days affected.
-> Planner: Final risk-adjusted intervals published.
Adaptive conformal updating applied (gamma=0.15); mean test interval multiplier 1.01, max 2.01.

base_stock policy: order-up-to = expected demand over 2 periods (lead time 1 + review 1) plus z=1.64 x forecast std (95% target). Five policies are compared on the same test window as a ladder: classical -> better forecast -> calibrated uncertainty -> Critic risk -> nowcast correction, so each agent's contribution can be separated.
